cases.question: List the mailing addresses and names of public high schools (SOC = 66) that have an SAT excellence rate above 0.25 and a K-12 to Ages 5–17 enrollment difference greater than the average such difference among locally funded schools.

Among schools that are either exclusively virtual (Virtual = 'F') or primarily virtual (Virtual = 'V'), find those where the absolute difference between K–12 enrollment and Ages 5–17 enrollment exceeds the county-wide average of such differences for virtual schools. Return the school name, city, county, and this enrollment difference, but only for schools located in counties with at least 3 virtual schools.

Find schools in Monterey County that are locally funded and have a free meal eligibility rate for students aged 5–17 higher than the average among all locally funded schools. Return the school name, street address, city, state, zip code, and phone number.

Find the names and phone numbers of schools that are locally funded, have an SAT excellence rate greater than 0.25, and where the difference between K–12 enrollment and enrollment for ages 5–17 exceeds the average such difference among all locally funded schools. Include only schools that opened after 1995 or closed before 2005.

Identify the cities in California that host exclusively virtual charter schools (Charter = 1 and Virtual = 'F') with an SAT excellence rate above 0.25, and where the school is located in a county that has at least one closed school. For these cities, return the city name, school name, and the eligible free meal rate for students aged 5–17.

List all cities that have at least one active magnet school serving a K-8 grade span and reporting FRPM data. For each city, show: (1) the total number of such schools, (2) the average percentage of K-12 students eligible for free or reduced-price meals, and (3) the average combined SAT score (Math + Reading + Writing) for those schools that have valid SAT data. Only include cities where the average FRPM eligibility rate is greater than 20%.

Find magnet schools in Los Angeles County where the SAT excellence rate is greater than 0.2 and the administrator’s first name starts with 'A' or 'J'. For these schools, return the school name, city, total SAT score (sum of reading, math, and writing), number of test takers, and the administrator's full name. Only include schools where all three SAT subject scores are available. Order results by total SAT score descending and limit to top 5.

Identify schools in Los Angeles County that are not charter schools, have a K-12 free meal eligibility rate below 18%, and whose difference between K-12 enrollment and Ages 5-17 enrollment exceeds the county-wide average for such schools. For these schools, return their full physical address and the administrator's primary contact information.

Find the mailing street address and school name of the school with the lowest SAT excellence rate among those that are locally funded and have an enrollment difference (K-12 minus ages 5–17) greater than the average such difference across all locally funded schools.

Find exclusively virtual schools (Virtual = 'F') in the county that has the highest number of closed schools. Among these schools, return the top 5 ranked by average reading score within that county, along with their eligible free meal rate for students aged 5–17.

Among charter schools that are either Active or Closed and located in counties that contain at least one State Special School (EdOpsCode = 'SSS'), find those with SAT excellence rates above 0.25. Return their charter number, school name, county, and eligible free rate for students aged 5–17, sorted by this rate in descending order.

Among schools in Los Angeles County that serve grades K–12 and have an SAT excellence rate above 0.15, find the one with the highest eligible free meal rate for students aged 5–17. Return its name, mailing city, administrator’s first name, charter status (Yes/No), and whether it is a magnet school.

Find the city and name of the magnet school with the highest number of students scoring 1500 or more on the SAT that is located in a county containing at least one locally funded charter school. Also return the school's phone number and opening date.

Find schools in Los Angeles County that are either locally funded charter schools or traditional public schools, and where the K-12 enrollment exceeds the enrollment for ages 5–17 by more than 400 students. Return the school name, city, administrator’s first and last name (if available), educational option name, and the calculated enrollment difference.

Identify public high schools in the county with the most closed schools that have a free meal eligibility rate (K-12) above 10% and rank among the top 3 by latitude within that county. Return the school name, full street address, phone number, and latitude.

Identify charter schools that are exclusively virtual and serve grades 9–12. Among these, find those located in counties where at least one school has an SAT excellence rate above 0.25. For each such school, return its name, charter number, county, and its rank in average math score within its county.

Find charter schools in California where the free meal eligibility rate for students aged 5–17 is higher than the lowest SAT excellence rate across all schools. Return the school name, city, and charter number.
List the names and cities of all active schools located in the county that has the highest number of closed schools, where each school serves students in grades 9 through 12.

Among directly funded charter schools that opened after January 1, 2000, find the city with the lowest total K–12 enrollment and return its name along with the average percent of eligible free meals (K–12) across all such schools in that city.

Identify the top two most common administrator first names among schools that are either High Schools (SOC = '66') or State Special Schools (EdOpsCode = 'SSS'), and for each of these administrators, list the schools they manage that have an FRPM Count (Ages 5–17) exceeding 1500. Include the school name, district, and the FRPM Count (Ages 5–17).

Among active schools in Santa Clara County that are charter schools, find those whose SAT excellence rate exceeds 0.25 and whose eligible free meal rate for students aged 5–17 is above the county-wide average for such schools. Return the school name, district, and the administrator’s first and last name.

Find schools that are either exclusively virtual (Virtual = 'F') or offer a magnet program (Magnet = 1), serve grades K through 8 (GSoffered = 'K-8'), and are located in counties with at least one school having more than 100 SAT test takers. For these schools, return their name, city, phone number, mailing city, and the eligible free meal rate for students aged 5–17. Only include schools with a valid phone number and non-null enrollment data for ages 5–17.

Find all charter schools in Los Angeles County that serve grades 9 through 12 and have more than 800 but fewer than 2,000 free meals for students aged 5–17. Return each school’s name, full mailing address (MailStreet, MailCity, MailState, MailZip), the administrator’s first and last name, and the eligible free rate for students aged 5–17.

Identify the names and mailing addresses of public Intermediate/Middle Schools in counties with the highest concentration of closed schools, where the school has an eligible free meal rate (K-12) above 10%, is not a magnet program, and ranks among the top 15 schools by enrollment (K-12).

List the names, counties, and cities of exclusively virtual schools (Virtual = 'F') that are among the top 3 in their county by total SAT score (sum of reading, math, and writing), where the county contains at least one active or closed District Community Day School (SOC = 69).

Identify schools in Los Angeles County that are non-charter, have a K-12 free meal eligibility rate below 25%, and serve more than 400 total enrolled students (K–12 plus ages 5–17). Among these, find the one with the highest average SAT Reading score and return its name, district, city, and that reading score.

Identify the city and full street address of the exclusively virtual charter school in California that is directly funded, opened after January 1, 2010, and has the lowest latitude among all such schools. Also report its lowest grade offered.

Identify the top 3 counties with the highest number of exclusively virtual schools (Virtual = 'F') that have an SAT excellence rate above 0.25 and a free meal eligibility rate for students aged 5–17 below 0.4. For each of these counties, list the county name and the count of such schools.

Identify charter schools that are directly funded and opened after January 1, 2005, which also rank among the top 3 in their county by average SAT Math score. For these schools, return the school name, city, phone number, and the full names of all listed administrators.

List the names and full physical addresses (Street, City, State, Zip) of active public high schools in Los Angeles County that are not charter schools, have an eligible free or reduced-price meal (FRPM) rate for K–12 students below 18%, and are among the top 5 schools with the highest FRPM Count (K–12). Only include schools where both enrollment and FRPM data are available.

Find the phone number of the charter high school (EILCode = 'HS') in Los Angeles County that has the highest SAT excellence rate among those whose K–12 enrollment is above the average K–12 enrollment of all charter high schools in the same county. Only include schools with valid SAT and enrollment data.

List exclusively virtual schools (Virtual = 'F') where the percentage of students eligible for free meals (K–12) exceeds 8%, and that either opened after 1990 or have no closure date (i.e., still active). For these schools, return their name, city, county, total K–12 enrollment, and their rank in average reading score within their county—only include schools ranked in the top 15 per county.

Among magnet schools in Los Angeles County that serve a grade span of K–8, K–9, or K–12, find the one with the lowest SAT excellence rate. Return its name, physical address (Street, City, State, Zip), FRPM count for students aged 5–17, and free meal eligibility rate for the same age group.

Identify schools in California that are either opened after 1995 or closed before 2005, are not charter schools, and have a free or reduced-price meal (FRPM) count (K–12) above the average FRPM count among all non-charter schools. For these schools, return their name, city, phone number, and the difference between their K–12 enrollment and 5–17 age enrollment.

List the names of exclusively virtual schools (Virtual = 'F') that are among the top 3 in their county by average SAT reading score and are located in a county that has at least one active or closed District Community Day School (SOC = 69).

Among schools administered by one of the two most common administrator first names, find those with an SAT excellence rate above 0.25. Return the school name, city, and the eligible free meal rate for students aged 5–17, sorted in descending order of that rate.

Identify charter schools in Santa Clara County that are locally funded and have an FRPM count (ages 5–17) greater than the average FRPM count for all locally funded charter schools in the county. For each such school, return its name, administrator’s full name, mailing city, and the difference between its K–12 enrollment and enrollment for ages 5–17.

Among public high schools (SOC = 66) in Los Angeles County that opened after 2005 and are not charter schools, find the one with the lowest SAT excellence rate. Return its full physical address (Street, City, State, Zip) and the eligible free meal rate for students aged 5–17.

Among locally funded charter schools that opened after January 1, 2005, identify those whose SAT excellence rate exceeds 0.25. For these schools, return the administrator’s full name, school name, city, and the eligible free rate for students aged 5–17. Only include schools where this free rate is above the average eligible free rate (for ages 5–17) across all such qualifying schools.

Find schools in California that are exclusively virtual and have an excellence rate below the statewide average for all exclusively virtual schools. Return their school name, city, and FRPM eligibility percentage for ages 5–17.

Find schools in Los Angeles County that are either exclusively virtual (Virtual = 'F') or primarily virtual (Virtual = 'V'), and have an SAT excellence rate above 0.2. For these schools, calculate the difference between their K–12 enrollment and enrollment for ages 5–17 from the FRPM data. Return the school name, full street address, virtual instruction type, SAT excellence rate, and the enrollment difference—but only if the difference is greater than 10 and both enrollment values are non-null. Prioritize schools with higher excellence rates.

Identify schools in counties with the highest number of closed schools that are locally funded charter schools, serve a K–8 grade span, and have a free meal eligibility rate (K–12) above the average for such schools. Return the school name, city, and its free meal eligibility percentage.

Identify schools where more than 10% of K–12 students are eligible for free meals and the total SAT score (sum of average reading, math, and writing) is below 1500. Return the school name, county, full physical address (street, city, state, zip), and excellence rate (NumGE1500 / NumTstTakr).

Among schools with locally funded charter status, identify those whose K-12 to ages 5–17 enrollment difference exceeds the average for such schools. For these schools, return the administrator's first name, district, and the school’s eligible free meal rate for students aged 5–17, but only if the administrator’s first name is among the two most common first names across all school administrators.

Identify schools in Los Angeles County that are exclusively virtual and have a K-12 enrollment exceeding the average K-12 enrollment of all locally funded schools. For these schools, return their name, full physical address, and the eligible free rate for students aged 5–17.

Identify schools in Los Angeles County that are charter-funded (either locally or directly), opened after January 1, 2005, and serve a K–8 grade span. For these schools, calculate the free meal eligibility rate for students aged 5–17, and return only those with a rate above 60%. Include the school name, city, and the calculated rate.

Identify exclusively virtual schools (Virtual = 'F') that rank among the top 3 in their county by total SAT score (sum of reading, math, and writing), and also have a difference greater than 50 between K-12 enrollment and Ages 5-17 enrollment. Return the school name, its total SAT score, county, and full street address.

Identify the county with the highest number of closed charter schools that are locally funded. For each such school in that county, return its name, closure date, and the percentage of students eligible for free meals (K-12).

Identify the top 5 schools with the highest SAT Math scores that are either magnet schools (Magnet = 1) or charter schools (Charter = 1). For each school, return its name, city, phone number, and the percentage of students aged 5–17 eligible for free meals. Only include schools where this percentage is greater than 20%.

Among active schools in Los Angeles County that serve grades K–12 (i.e., GSserved = 'K-12'), find the one with the lowest combined SAT score (reading + math + writing). Return its name, administrator’s last name, charter number (or 'N/A' if not a charter), and the percentage of students aged 5–17 eligible for free meals.

Identify schools that are exclusively virtual (Virtual = 'F'), have at least one student with a total SAT score of 1500 or higher (NumGE1500 > 0), and are located in counties where more than 20% of charter schools are locally funded. Return the school name, its county, and the percentage of locally funded charter schools in that county.

Identify schools in California that either opened after 1990 or have no closure date, offer a grade span that includes high school (i.e., ends with '12'), and are associated with both FRPM and SAT data. For these schools, calculate the SAT excellence rate and the eligible free meal rate for students aged 5–17. Return the school name, district, county, both rates, and the number of test takers, but only for schools where the SAT excellence rate exceeds 0.1 and the free meal rate exceeds 0.2.

Identify charter schools in California that are locally funded and have a K-12 enrollment at least 50 students greater than their Ages 5-17 enrollment. Among these, return only those that rank in the top 3 within their county based on the eligible free or reduced price meal rate for K-12. For each qualifying school, provide its name, city, charter number, and the calculated FRPM rate.

In Los Angeles County, find the number of active or closed public schools that are not charter schools, serve a grade span of K–12 (GSoffered = 'K-12'), and have more than 500 students eligible for free or reduced-price meals in grades K–12. Group the results by city and only include cities with at least two such schools.

Among magnet schools in counties with at least one school offering exclusively virtual instruction (Virtual = 'F'), find the top 3 cities with the lowest total K-12 enrollment. For each of these cities, return the city name, the number of such magnet schools, and the average eligible free meal rate (Free Meal Count (K-12) / Enrollment (K-12)) across those schools.

Among charter schools in Santa Clara County with an SAT excellence rate above 0.25, identify the top 3 cities (by total K-12 enrollment) and return their average eligible free meal rate for students aged 5–17.

Identify the full address (Street, City, State, Zip) of the non-charter school in Los Angeles County with the lowest excellence rate among schools that have an eligible free meal rate for K–12 students below 1%.

Identify the cities in counties with the highest number of closed schools that also have at least one active District Community Day School, and return the free meal eligibility rate for students aged 5–17 in those cities.

Identify exclusively virtual magnet schools in California that opened after 2005 and are among the top 3 in their county by average SAT Math score. For each such school, return its name, city, phone number, and the lowest grade it serves.

Find schools in Los Angeles County that are charter schools and have an administrator whose first name is among the two most common administrator first names statewide. Return the school name, administrator’s full name, phone number, and the percentage of students eligible for free meals (K–12).

Find schools in Los Angeles County with a mailing city of 'Los Angeles' that have an SAT excellence rate above 0.15 and serve high school grades. Return the school name, phone number, and the percentage of students aged 5–17 eligible for free or reduced-price meals.

Among exclusively virtual schools (Virtual = 'F') in California that opened in or after 2005 and have at least 30 test takers, identify the top 5 ranked by their eligible free or reduced price meal rate for grades K–12. Return the school name, city, county, number of test takers, average SAT writing score, and the calculated FRPM rate.

Find the three cities with the lowest total K-12 enrollment that contain at least one exclusively virtual school (Virtual = 'F') ranked among the top 5 in its county by average reading score. Return each city’s name, the number of such schools, and the earliest open date among them.

Identify exclusively virtual schools (Virtual = 'F') with an SAT excellence rate above 0.2. Among these, return those whose eligible free meal rate for students aged 5–17 exceeds the average such rate across all locally funded schools. For each qualifying school, list its name, city, and the difference between its K–12 and ages 5–17 enrollment.

Identify the names and full mailing addresses of exclusively virtual schools located in Los Angeles County that have an SAT excellence rate above 0.25 and a free meal eligibility rate for students aged 5–17 higher than the average among all locally funded schools.

Identify charter schools in districts whose names start with 'San' that have an SAT excellence rate above the average excellence rate of all locally funded charter schools. Return their charter numbers, school names, and rank them by their writing scores in descending order.

Among K–12 schools with enrollment (K–12) over 400 and located in counties where at least one school has a mailing city of 'Fresno', find the school with the lowest total SAT score (sum of Math, Reading, and Writing). Return its grade span offered, county, free meal eligibility rate for students aged 5–17, and the name of its top administrator (first and last name).

Among active schools with an SAT excellence rate above 0.25, find the one with the lowest combined SAT score (Reading + Math + Writing). Return its name, county, website, and the eligible free meal rate for students aged 5–17.

List all closed schools in the county that has the highest number of closed schools, where the school is located in a city with total K–12 enrollment (across all schools) under 5,000 students. Return the school name, closure date, and city.
Find the names and mailing zip codes of non-magnet schools in the county with the most closed schools that have a FRPM count (Ages 5–17) greater than 100.

Identify the top 3 active charter schools (Charter = 1) with the highest average SAT Math scores. For each school, return its name, city, charter number, and the percentage of students eligible for free meals (K-12).

Identify schools that are either exclusively virtual or primarily virtual, located in the county with the highest number of closed schools, and have a difference greater than 50 between their K-12 enrollment and ages 5–17 enrollment. For these schools, return their name, city, full street address, and their rank within the county based on average math SAT scores.

Among schools with an SAT excellence rate above 0.25, return the school name, county, and eligible free or reduced price meal rate for students aged 5–17, but only for schools in counties where the number of directly funded charter schools exceeds the number of locally funded ones. Limit to the top 3 results by FRPM rate (ages 5–17) in descending order.

Among locally funded high schools (SOC = 66) in active districts, find those whose FRPM count for ages 5–17 exceeds the average FRPM count for this same group. For each such school, return its name, city, and the percentage of students eligible for free meals in K–12.

Among schools in California that are classified as high schools (EILCode = 'HS') and located in counties with names starting with 'M', find the one with the lowest SAT excellence rate. Return its full physical address, administrator's last name, and the percentage of students aged 5–17 eligible for free meals.

Identify schools in Los Angeles County that are directly funded charter schools with a K–12 free meal eligibility rate below 18%, and whose difference between K–12 enrollment and Ages 5–17 enrollment exceeds the average enrollment difference across all directly funded charter schools in Los Angeles County. Return the school name, city, phone number, and this enrollment difference.

Find schools that are exclusively virtual (Virtual = 'F') and serve a K-12 grade span. Among these, return only those whose difference between K-12 enrollment and Ages 5-17 enrollment exceeds the average such difference across all locally funded schools. For each qualifying school, list its name, city, website, and total enrollment (K-12).

Among schools with an SAT excellence rate above 0.25, identify those located in counties where at least one of the two most common administrator first names appears. For these schools, compute the eligible free meal rate for students aged 5–17 and return the school name, county, and this rate, ordered from highest to lowest rate.

Among schools with a total SAT score (sum of Math, Reading, and Writing averages) above 1500, find the two most common administrator first names. For each of these names, list all associated schools that are magnet programs (Magnet = 1).

Identify exclusively virtual charter schools in California that opened after 2005 and have an SAT excellence rate greater than 0.2. For these schools, return the school name, city, phone number, charter funding type, and the eligible free meal rate for students aged 5–17. Only include schools where both SAT and FRPM data are available.

Among schools located in the five counties with the lowest total K–12 enrollment, identify those where the SAT excellence rate exceeds 0.25. For each such school, return its name, the administrator’s full name (first and last), the type of education offered, and the eligible free meal rate for students aged 5–17.

Identify the names and websites of exclusively virtual charter schools in the county with the highest number of closed schools, where the school's free meal eligibility rate for students aged 5–17 exceeds 20%.

Identify the top 5 exclusively virtual schools (Virtual = 'F') in each county based on average SAT reading scores. Return the school name, city, county, administrator’s first and last name (if available), phone number, and average reading score. Only include schools that have valid SAT reading scores.

Identify the top 3 cities in California with the lowest total K-12 enrollment that also contain at least one active school with an SAT reading score above 500. For each such city, return the city name, the number of qualifying schools, and the highest SAT math score among those schools.

Among charter schools in Santa Clara County with an SAT excellence rate above 0.25, find the city with the lowest total K-12 enrollment and return its complete physical address (Street, City, State, Zip).
Among all expansion-type sets that have Japanese translations, find the Italian-translated names of cards illustrated by Chippy, ordered by descending converted mana cost.

Find the French foreign names of all cards illustrated by John Avon that have a black border color, do not have multiple faces (side IS NULL), and belong to sets released after January 1, 2010. Among these, only include cards that are either non-foil-only or have no powerful foil identifiers (i.e., lack both cardKingdomId and cardKingdomFoilId).

List the Italian name of the card with the highest converted mana cost that is legal in Commander format without a content warning and belongs to an expansion set that has a Japanese translation. The set must also appear in Brazilian Portuguese translations.
Find the name and artist of the promotional card that has the most rulings. Also, indicate whether its set has a Korean translation.

Identify the IDs and artists of cards that are legal in the Commander format, have unknown power (either NULL or '*'), feature a 1997 frame style, and were illustrated by an artist whose name appears in rulings associated with cards that have content warnings.

List the Italian names of cards that have rulings and were illustrated by artists who also created cards available in Phyrexian. For each card, indicate whether it has sensitive content, and order the results by converted mana cost descending.

Find the artist who illustrated the fewest cards that are legal in the 'commander' format and have an Italian translation. Return the English name, Italian name, and set name for all cards by this artist that have an Italian translation.

Find the names and artists of all mythic rare cards that are legal in the Commander format, have unknown power (either NULL or '*'), and feature the 'boros' watermark. Additionally, include the set name each card belongs to, but only for sets released after January 1, 2015.

Identify textless cards illustrated by either John Avon or Aleksi Briclot that have non-powerful foil availability. For these cards, determine their legal status in the Legacy format and whether they appear in any set that has a Korean translation.

Find the IDs and artists of cards that are legal in the 'pauper' format, available in paper, illustrated by either 'Erica Yang' or 'Jim Pavelec', and belong to sets released after January 1, 2020. Among these, return only those with unknown power (either NULL or '*').
Among cards that are legal in the Legacy format and illustrated by Stephen Daniele, what percentage have unknown power (i.e., power is null or '*')?
Find the artist who illustrated the fewest borderless cards that are banned in any format and also appear in a starter deck. Return the artist's name and the count of such cards.

Among cards with the 'legendary' frame effect that are legal in the 'premodern' format and have no multiple faces, find the Italian-translated names of those with the highest converted mana cost within each set they belong to.
Identify the names of cards that are both incredibly powerful foils and have alternative language versions in Russian, while also belonging to sets released in 2007 with a converted mana cost of 3.

Find the names of cards illustrated by artists who have also created cards in the 'Coldsnap' set, where those cards are legal in the 'pauper' format, available in 'paper', and have an EDHRec rank below 100. Return only the top 5 such cards by converted mana cost (highest first).

Find the names of all borderless cards that have rulings and are part of sets with Italian translations. Return only those whose set has a baseSetSize greater than 200, ordered by ruling date (oldest first), and limit to 5 results.

Among all cards with full artwork and a black border, what percentage are only available in online game variations? Additionally, for these cards, list their original release dates and legal play formats if they are mythic rarity and have a defined release date.

Identify the top three most frequently occurring visual frame effects among cards that are either banned or restricted in any format, have at least one ruling (regardless of content), and belong to sets that include Italian translations. Exclude cards with NULL frame effects.

Find the names of cards illustrated by 'Aleksi Briclot' that are legal in the 'Legacy' format, have a black border, and appear in starter decks. For each such card, also return the set name it belongs to.

Among cards illustrated by artists who have worked on Phyrexian-language cards, count how many have unknown power (NULL or '*') and are either textless or have a normal layout. Exclude cards that are only available in foil (i.e., require hasFoil = 0).

List the distinct names of cards that are either 'Serra Angel' or 'Shrine Keeper', illustrated by artists who also designed cards in the 'Coldsnap' set, and that have a German foreign type entry. Return the results ordered by converted mana cost in descending order.

Among cards illustrated by Allen Williams that are legal in the 'commander' format, identify those with the highest converted mana cost. For each such card, return its name, frame version, and whether it is banned in any format.

Identify artists who have illustrated at least one card that is both textless and part of an incredibly powerful foil (where both cardKingdomId and cardKingdomFoilId are not null), and whose cards include at least one with a 2015 frame version and an EDHRec rank below 100. For these artists, list all foreign languages in which any of their cards have non-null flavor text.

Among all cards illustrated by artists who have also designed cards with non-powerful foils (i.e., missing either cardKingdomId or cardKingdomFoilId), what percentage of those cards that are legal in the 'commander' format do not have a content warning?

Identify cards that (1) are available in at least one non-paper format (e.g., 'mtgo' or 'arena'), (2) have an EDHRec rank within the top 50, (3) were illustrated by either 'Chippy', 'Jeremy Jarvis', or 'Daren Bader', and (4) belong to sets of type 'expansion' or 'core'. For these cards, return their name, artist, set name, converted mana cost, and whether they are legal in the 'Commander' format.

What is the percentage of cards that are legal in the 'premodern' format, have the exact ruling text 'This is a triggered mana ability.', do not have multiple faces, and belong to sets with Russian translations, that also appear in Chinese Simplified foreign data? The percentage should be computed over all such qualifying cards, regardless of whether they have foreign data entries.

Among cards illustrated by Adam Rex that are of uncommon rarity and have at least one ruling, compute the percentage that are legal in the Commander format and do not have a content warning. Only consider cards that appear in sets released after January 1, 2005.

Find the names of all Creature-type cards illustrated by Kev Walker that belong to Russian-translated sets with the largest base set size, and return them ordered by their converted mana cost in descending order.

Identify the names and frame versions of cards illustrated by 'Allen Williams' that are legal in the 'commander' format, have unknown power (either NULL or '*'), and belong to sets with expansion type 'expansion'. Among these, return only those with the highest converted mana cost within their respective sets.
Among cards illustrated by D. Alexander Gregory that are legal in the Commander format and have full artwork, what percentage do not carry a content warning?

Among cards that are either restricted or banned in any competitive format and have a text box, find the most common visual frame effect for non-powerful foil cards (where at least one of cardKingdomId or cardKingdomFoilId is missing) that are not multi-faced and belong to sets released after 2010.

Among all cards illustrated by John Avon that are legal in the Legacy format and have a ruling issued on February 1, 2007, calculate the percentage that are of 'rare' rarity. Additionally, return the total count of such cards, the count of rare ones, and the average converted mana cost of the rare subset.

Among cards that either have no power value or are marked with '*' for power, find those that are banned in any format and have a white border. For these cards, list their foreign names in French along with whether they carry a content warning.

Find the number of distinct non-textless cards illustrated by 'Volkan Baǵa' that have at least one ruling issued after January 1, 2020, and whose frame effect is among those that appear more than once in the set of incredibly powerful foils—defined as cards where both cardKingdomId and cardKingdomFoilId are not null.

Identify the names of cards that meet all of the following criteria: (1) illustrated by either Jeremy Jarvis or Chippy, (2) belong to the set named 'Coldsnap', (3) have an Italian-translated version, and (4) have a convertedManaCost greater than the average convertedManaCost of all cards in the 'Coldsnap' set. Return the results ordered by convertedManaCost in descending order.

Among all sets with Japanese translations, identify those that are exclusively non-foil and have a base set size greater than the average base set size of Russian-translated sets. For cards in these qualifying sets, find the percentage that are legal in the 'commander' format and do not carry a content warning, but only consider cards released with the 2015 frame version and ranked below 150 on EDHRec.

Find the French foreign name of the card with the highest converted mana cost that is legal in the 'duel' format, has rarity 'rare', and belongs to a set that has an Italian translation and a base set size under 100.

Identify all cards illustrated by 'Allen Williams' that are legal in the 'commander' format and available on Magic: The Gathering Online. For each such card, return its name, frame version, and whether it has a content warning.

Among cards that are part of duel deck 'a' and have unknown power (either NULL or '*'), find those that belong to sets with Japanese translations. For these cards, list their names ordered by the earliest ruling date, and include only those whose sets are available on Magic: The Gathering Online.
